description: MoonBase Planner helps identify places on Earth that are similar to potential locations on the Moon and Mars. It compares factors such as terrain, temperature, surface conditions, and environmental data to find the best Earth analog locations. These sites can be used to test space equipment, technologies, and mission activities before deployment in space. Our goal is to make future Moon and Mars missions safer, smarter, and more practical.
summary:
MoonBase Planner – Planetary Analog Finder

MoonBase Planner is a web-based tool that helps identify Earth locations that can serve as analogs for potential Moon and Mars landing sites or base environments. The idea is to study Earth locations with similar physical and environmental characteristics so that technologies and mission activities can be tested before being deployed in space.

Users can select the Moon or Mars and explore target locations based on factors such as terrain, slope, temperature, surface conditions, geology, and aridity. The system compares these characteristics with Earth locations and generates a similarity score. The results are displayed through an interactive map and comparison dashboard, helping users understand why a particular location is considered a useful analog.

The project uses a web frontend, Python FastAPI backend, structured datasets, and a prototype scoring system. It provides APIs for analyzing targets, comparing locations, retrieving Earth analogs, and accessing data sources.

MoonBase Planner does not claim that Earth locations are identical to the Moon or Mars. Instead, it provides a practical way to discover and study useful terrestrial analogs for rover testing, astronaut training, equipment testing, navigation experiments, and geological research.

Our goal is to make planetary exploration planning more accessible and support safer, smarter, and better-prepared future Moon and Mars missions.
details:
MoonBase Planner – Planetary Analog Finder

MoonBase Planner is a web-based application designed to identify and study locations on Earth that can serve as terrestrial analogs for potential Moon and Mars landing sites or base environments. The main idea is to find Earth environments with similar physical and environmental characteristics so that technologies, equipment, and mission activities can be tested on Earth before being deployed in space.

Future Moon and Mars missions involve high costs and risks. Testing everything directly in space is difficult and expensive. Therefore, suitable Earth environments can be used to test rover technologies, navigation systems, scientific instruments, astronaut procedures, geological research methods, communication systems, and other mission technologies.

The user starts by selecting a planetary target such as the Moon or Mars. The system then analyzes characteristics such as terrain, slope, temperature, surface conditions, geology, and aridity. These characteristics are compared with available Earth analog locations. A prototype similarity score is calculated based on the selected characteristics, and the Earth locations can then be ranked according to their similarity. The results are presented through the web interface, comparison views, and data-driven visualizations.

The project follows a modular architecture. The frontend is developed using HTML5, CSS, and JavaScript. HTML provides the structure of the webpages, CSS controls the layout and visual design, and JavaScript provides interactivity and communicates with the backend. The current frontend contains index.html for the home page, explorer.html for the main exploration interface, and about.html for project information, along with separate CSS and JavaScript folders.

The backend is developed using Python and FastAPI. FastAPI provides the REST API layer through which the frontend communicates with the analysis system. Uvicorn is used as the server for running the FastAPI application. The backend also uses CORS middleware to allow frontend-backend communication during local development and StaticFiles to serve the frontend and data files. Python libraries such as pathlib, os, and sys are used for file paths and system-level operations.

The project contains separate folders for backend, frontend, data, models, and scripts, making the system easier to maintain and extend. The data folder stores project data and resources, while the models and scripts folders provide a structure for future data-processing and machine-learning functionality.

The application provides API endpoints for functions such as checking the system health, retrieving Earth analog locations, analyzing planetary targets, comparing locations, accessing processed analog data, and viewing data sources and provenance. FastAPI also automatically provides interactive API documentation through the /docs page.

The project uses a prototype similarity-scoring approach. Factors can include terrain, slope, temperature, geology, aridity, and surface conditions. Example prototype weights are terrain 25%, slope 15%, temperature 15%, geology 20%, aridity 15%, and surface conditions 10%. These weights are intended for the prototype and are not presented as scientifically validated values.

The complete workflow can be described as: User → Select Moon/Mars → Select or analyze target → Extract planetary characteristics → Compare with Earth locations → Calculate similarity → Rank analog locations → Display results → Support mission planning.

The project can support applications such as rover testing, astronaut training, equipment testing, navigation experiments, geological studies, and mission preparation. For example, an Earth location with dry, rocky, or challenging terrain may provide a useful environment for testing specific rover or navigation technologies.

An important scientific limitation is that MoonBase Planner does not claim that an Earth location is identical to the Moon or Mars. Instead, it identifies locations that share selected characteristics and may therefore be useful terrestrial analogs for particular mission activities. The similarity score is a prototype decision-support mechanism and should not be treated as a scientifically validated statement of planetary equivalence.

The project is designed to be expanded in the future by integrating real NASA and other space-agency datasets, digital elevation models, geological information, temperature data, satellite imagery, lunar South Pole information, Mars terrain data, GIS analysis, advanced machine-learning models, and 3D terrain visualization. With these improvements, the system could become a more advanced platform for planetary analog discovery and mission preparation.

The main goal of MoonBase Planner is to make planetary exploration planning more accessible and understandable by combining planetary data, Earth analog information, transparent similarity scoring, APIs, and interactive visualization. By helping researchers and mission planners discover useful Earth analog environments, the project aims to support safer, smarter, and better-prepared future Moon and Mars missions.

Technology Stack: Python 3.10, FastAPI, Uvicorn, HTML5, CSS, JavaScript, REST APIs, structured datasets, and a modular architecture for data processing and future machine-learning integration.

Project Structure: backend/ contains the FastAPI application and API routes; frontend/ contains index.html, explorer.html, about.html, CSS, and JavaScript; data/ contains project datasets and resources; models/ is used for model-related components; scripts/ contains supporting scripts; requirements.txt contains Python dependencies; README.md contains project documentation.

The application can be run locally using a Python virtual environment. After activating the environment and installing the dependencies from requirements.txt, the backend can be started using “python backend\run.py”. The website is then available at http://localhost:8000 and the interactive FastAPI documentation is available at http://localhost:8000/docs.

The complete source code and project documentation are available on GitHub at https://github.com/NotGoblin01/moonX.

GitHub Repository: https://github.com/NotGoblin01/moonX

Overall, MoonBase Planner connects Earth-based testing with future planetary exploration by providing a practical platform for discovering and comparing terrestrial analog environments for Moon and Mars missions.
